notes:
ACCESS: https://www.walmart.com/ reached DIRECTLY with probe.fetch()/curl_cffi - HTTP 200 on the homepage, robots.txt, sitemap_category.xml, sitemap_browse_fst.xml and ~195 /browse/ category pages. No proxy, no reader, no browser automation, no campaign parameter. Walmart's bot management did intermittently serve a 'Robot or human?' interstitial; that was handled by detecting the string and retrying on a different curl_cffi fingerprint after a back-off, never by defeating a challenge. Roughly 15 of ~195 page fetches needed a retry. ROBOTS: https://www.walmart.com/robots.txt fetched FIRST (HTTP 200). NO ClaudeBot / anthropic-ai / Claude-Web group exists; the only named agents are Adsbot-Google, Mediapartners-Google (both empty groups) and Slurp (Crawl-delay: 5, not us). No Crawl-delay applies to us; probe.py's 2s/host gap was honoured throughout. The governing 'User-agent: *' group disallows /api/, /search, /search/api/wpa, */api/wpa, */midas/*, /store/category/, /store/ajax/*, /store/electrode/api/*, /cp/-201, /cp/-302, /cp/-306, /cp/-309, /cp/-506, /cp/-509, /cp/api/*, /electrode/api/logger, /typeahead/, /giftregistry/, /account/, /orders, /es/, /feeds/*, /sp/*, /c/kp/*/page/*, /solutions/, /wmflows/, /tealeaf, /msp, */undefined/*, /store/*/search and /storeLocator/. NONE of those was requested: no /api/ endpoint, no /search path and no /cp/-NNN page was ever fetched. Everything used is under /browse/ or /cp//, neither of which is disallowed, plus the two sitemaps robots.txt itself advertises. There is no 'Disallow: *?' rule, so the two verification fetches that carried ?max_price= / ?min_price= (below) were permitted; no recorded link carries a parameter. TREE SOURCE: (1) https://www.walmart.com/sitemap_category.xml (12,344 /cp/ hub URLs) and https://www.walmart.com/sitemap_browse_fst.xml (49,252 /browse/ URLs) - both declared in robots.txt - gave the taxonomy id-paths, which Walmart encodes directly in the URL (e.g. 4044_539095_2505058_1549287 = Home > Bath > Bathroom Accessories > Soap Dishes). Two bathroom roots were isolated: 4044_539095 (Home > Bath) and 1072864_1045879 (Home Improvement > Bathroom Renovation). (2) The authoritative navigation came from each page's OWN server-rendered __NEXT_DATA__ - props.pageProps.initialData.contentLayout PillsModule.pillsV2 is Walmart's own category pill nav, and searchResult.shelfData.shelfName is the site's own canonical shelf path. Parentage was taken from shelfName and breadCrumb, never from URL shape - which mattered: /browse/home/towel-bars/4044_539095_1230879_1230856 is served under the Home>Bath id-path but its own shelf is 'Home Improvement:Bathroom Renovation:Bathroom Hardware:Towel Bars'. 195 nodes were crawled; ~165 resolved to a real shelf. COUNT SOURCE AND THE CAP - THE CENTRAL FINDING: Walmart renders its total in the listing H1 as totalItemCountDisplay. Below 1,000 it renders the EXACT figure (verified in raw HTML: the Hookless Shower Curtains page literally contains

Shop Hookless Shower Curtains for Easy Bath(244)

); at or above 1,000 it renders the string '(1000+)' and paginationV2.maxPage is pinned at 25, i.e. the site itself refuses to state a number and caps browsing at ~1,000 items. THE PAYLOAD FIELD IS NOT A SAFE SUBSTITUTE. searchResult.aggregatedCount is PROVEN capped and unreliable at scale by exactly the OTTO test: it returns the identical sentinel 900010 for BOTH the entire Bath department AND its single child 'Shower Curtains & Accessories' - two nodes of visibly different size reporting the same round figure - and it reports 889,003 for 'Fabric Shower Curtains', i.e. 98.8% of the whole department, plus 453,567 for 'Extra Long Shower Curtains'. Those are search-recall numbers, not category memberships. WHAT I DID VERIFY ABOUT IT (disclosed in full): on nodes whose H1 renders an exact figure, aggregatedCount equals that figure exactly (32=32, 244=244, 481=481, 555=555, 618=618, 826=826 ...). And it behaves additively across DISJOINT price facets on two nodes of very different size - Bathroom Tumblers base 1287 vs max_price=15 -> 984 plus min_price=15 -> 316 (sum 1300, +1.0% from boundary/variant pricing), and Soap Dishes base 32547 vs max_price=20 -> 28799 plus min_price=20 -> 3949 (sum 32748, +0.6%). So it is coherent, but coherence is not enough against a proven 900010 sentinel and an 889,003 absurdity. DECISION (rule 26, OTTO precedent): a qty is recorded ONLY where the listing page's own H1 renders an exact number. Every node whose page renders '(1000+)' carries NO qty and sits in review[] with its exact URL and the aggregatedCount quoted as a reference value only, explicitly labelled unreliable. That is why 22 leaves carry counts and ~100 bathroom nodes do not. A plausible wrong number is worse than an honest gap. COUNTS DISCRIMINATE: 24, 32, 32, 51, 57, 65, 92, 115, 122, 146, 149, 279, 315, 340, 416, 465, 481, 555, 618, 667, 718, 826 - no repeats of a round figure, no site-wide constant, and every one matches its own page's H1 and shelfName. DEDUP (OPTION 1): already_extracted() was run on all 195 crawled URLs. ONE exact hit: /browse/home-improvement/bathroom-vanities/1072864_1045879_1230843_9176721 is in Furniture.xlsx for Walmart US as 'Bathroom Vanities'. It stays in Furniture. Blind spot (a) was then worked deliberately: the alias /browse/home/bathroom-vanities/4044_539095_5547362_9176721 resolves to the SAME shelfName and the same total but is absent from the URL-exact index, and so are all the vanity children (Single Sink 430, with Tops 619, without Tops 126, with Mirrors, Small, and the four by-size cuts). Recording any of those would re-extract products the Furniture pass already took, so ALL vanity nodes are in review[], none in rows[]. The index holds 74 walmart.com URLs; no other bathroom node matched any of them. Walmart US is single-locale on this host (the /es/ path is robots-disallowed and was not touched), so blind spots (b)/(c) do not apply. ROUTED OUT: all bath towels, hand towels, washcloths, bath sheets, towel sets, beach towels and beach blankets; all textile bathroom rugs, rug sets and bath-mat runners; all shower curtains, curtain sets, liners and kids' shower curtains -> TEXTILE (rules 15/16/20). Vanity Lights & Bathroom Light Fixtures -> LIGHTING (rule 19), confirmed by its own shelf 'Home:Decor:Lighting & Light Fixtures:Wall Lights & Fixtures'. Where an exact rendered qty existed for a routed node it is carried into review[] so the Textile pass can use it. KEPT IN BATHROOM despite a textile-ish name: Bathtub Mats (non-slip PVC/suction in-tub mats, rule 16) - capped, so no qty; Curved Shower Curtain Rods and the Shower Hooks & Rods / Shower Curtain Hooks & Rings nodes (hardware, rule 17); Towel Bars, Racks, Rings, Hooks, Warmers and Hand Towel Holders (hardware, rule 15/17). EXCLUDED AS NOT BATHROOM (each named in review[] so nothing is silently skipped): the whole Bathroom Plumbing supply branch (pipes, valves, drains, hoses, faucet/sink/shower spares, plumbing tools), water heaters, Waste & Sewage Equipment, Utility Fixtures (laundry sinks/faucets/countertops), Utility Sinks, Bath Fans, Backsplashes (whose own shelf is Kitchen Renovation), toilet cistern spares, and the Household Essentials cleaning lines (toilet brushes, plungers). Kids' Bathroom is a shop-by-room re-cut of already-covered bath products and is withheld under rule 28. Facet, finish, brand, size and material re-cuts (Bathroom Sinks by Brand/Finish, Kraus, Copper/Stainless sinks, Ceramic/Gold soap dispensers, Ceramic Toothbrush Holder, the four vanity size cuts, Fabric/White/Extra Long/Christmas shower curtains) are NOT subcategories and are withheld to avoid double counting. KNOWN GAPS, STATED HONESTLY: (a) ~100 genuine Bathroom nodes carry no qty because Walmart caps its own displayed total at '(1000+)'; that includes large, clearly-real categories such as Bathroom Mirrors, Medicine Cabinets, Shower Doors, Shower Heads, Shower Enclosures, Toilet Paper Holders, Towel Bars, Soap Dishes, Soap Dispensers, Toothbrush Holders, Bathroom Shelves and Bathroom Cabinets. (b) Several catIds harvested from the SEO browse sitemap return an empty result at the slug/id combination the sitemap publishes (all-toilet-seats, hard-toilet-seat, children-toilet-seats, bidet-toilet-seats, toilet-seats-and-lids, toilet-bowls, pipes-fittings, plumbing-tools, aerators-and-adaptors, shower-head-replacement-parts and ~10 others); they are stale SEO paths, so the Toilet Seats branch is represented only by Cushioned Toilet Seats (32), the one child that resolved. (c) Kid's Bath Rugs renders two different exact totals (228 and 236) at two catIds for the same shelf, so no figure is asserted for it. COUNT VOLATILITY DISCLOSED: Walmart's totals are live marketplace inventory and drift by the minute. Every one of the 22 recorded leaves was RE-READ a second time at the end of the session and each row now carries that second, single-window reading. The drift observed between the two readings was small and one-directional-random: Wall Mounted Bathroom Sinks 416->418, Bidet Faucets 315->316, Alcove Bathtubs 115->114, Freestanding Tubs 618->617, Shower Stalls 279->282, Bidets 481->480, One Piece Toilets 667->668, Cushioned Toilet Seats 32->33, Automatic Soap Dispensers 718->716, Curved Shower Curtain Rods 555->557, Undermount Bathroom Sinks 149->148; the other eleven were identical. One node, Bathroom Trash Cans, was seen at 39 in an intermediate read and 32 in both the first and final reads, so it is the most volatile of the set. These are real inventory movements, not measurement error - stated so the figures are read as a point-in-time snapshot (2026-09-01).
